summary: String.slice copies a range of UTF-16 code units without modifying the string.
documentation: String.slice copies a range of UTF-16 code units without modifying the string. A negative start counts backward from the end; an omitted end includes the remainder. End is exclusive and out-of-range bounds are clamped.
inputs: An object with text (ASCII string) and count (integer 0..100).
caution: slice(-0) means slice(0), which returns the whole string. Handle a requested count of zero explicitly. UTF-16 positions are not grapheme boundaries.
scenarios: Show the final four characters of a support reference.
Preview the tail of a long ASCII filename.
Display a short identifier suffix in a compact activity list.
title: Take a reference suffix
problem: Input is {text, count}. Return the last count characters of the ASCII string, or the entire string when count exceeds its length. Return an empty string when count is zero.
hint: Handle zero before calling slice with a negative start.
goal: Use String.slice() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
